Theme

School & learning

teach verb

also taught, teach someone something, teaching

classical

Cic. Pis. 30: aliquem litterās (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 32

doceō, docēre, docuī, doctum

verb, second conjugation, with two accusatives (whom and what)

The person taught and the thing taught are both accusative: puerōs elementa docet. It is also “show, inform” (see explain).

Other words

  • ērudiō, ērudīre, ērudīvī, ērudītum — educate, instruct

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.156 (Lewis & Short)

    Literally “take the roughness out”: to educate, more formal than docēre.

  • īnstituō, īnstituere, īnstituī, īnstitūtum — train, bring up

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. ērudiō: with īnstituere

    To ground someone in something, to train; its everyday senses are “set up, begin, decide”.

Examples

  • fās est et ab hoste docērī

    it is right to be taught even by an enemyOv. Met. 4.428

  • Praeceptor sedet in cathedrā; discipulī in subselliīs; ille docet, hī discunt.

    The teacher sits in his chair, the pupils on the benches; he teaches, they learn.Comen. OP 97

See also learn, teacher, lesson, pupil, explain.
